chunks: This is the sentence whose value cannot be assessed, with which no wise saying can be weighed and with which no other sentence can be matched.

key_terms.السَّيِّدُ الرِّضْيُ: As-Sayyid ar-Raḍī, a prominent Shia scholar and compiler of Nahj al-Balagha

ai.seo_question: What makes a specific word in the Quran or Hadith inestimable and unmatched?
ai.summary: Sharif al-Raḍī elevates this specific word—often interpreted as the divine name or the Quranic opening—to a status beyond material valuation or comparative wisdom, highlighting its unique ontological weight in Shia rhetorical tradition. This description underscores the concept that true nobility is derived from spiritual and intellectual achievements rather than worldly metrics, a core theme in the *Nahj al-Balagha*. The phrasing reflects the Mu'tazili-influenced emphasis on the rationality and precision of divine speech.

en.sayed-ali-raza: This is the sentence whose value cannot be assessed, with which no wise saying can be weighed and with which no other sentence can be matched.
